claim: Every app PRD should define the five-second gotcha moment that makes the product promise immediately understandable.
mechanism: A concrete proof moment aligns product scope, acquisition creative, onboarding, and conversion around one visible outcome.

claim: Design and validate the viral promise and creative before expanding the product around it.
mechanism: Content-first testing exposes whether a promise earns attention before additional build effort and keeps the product matched to acquisition intent.

claim: Use a dedicated research identity that behaves like the target customer so platform recommendations surface relevant creators.
mechanism: Repeated niche-consistent viewing and engagement turns the recommendation feed into a candidate-discovery surface; candidates still require native evidence and compliance review.

claim: Test concise creator outreach beginning with Paid promo? and a bounded daily send cap.
mechanism: The opening makes commercial intent explicit while one product sentence and one invitation reduce reading cost; reply, agreement, post, and paid outcome rates decide whether it works.

claim: Test a three-day free trial only on the annual subscription package.
mechanism: Restricting trial access to annual packaging may shift plan selection and retained revenue; conversion, refund, churn, and contribution margin must be measured by app and experiment.

claim: Let onboarding execute the gotcha, then place the result reveal at the paywall.
mechanism: Users invest context and observe progress before the value-bearing result is revealed; activation, paywall conversion, refunds, and retention determine whether the sequence helps rather than frustrates.

claim: Use high-running competitor ads to form original replication hypotheses about hook, proof, pacing, offer, and CTA.
mechanism: Separating why an ad works from its protected assets enables an original treatment that tests the same mechanism without copying brand identity or creative files.

claim: Run product construction and a high-volume UGC exploration lane in parallel.
mechanism: Independent build and acquisition work shorten the feedback cycle, provided every creative has an experiment ID and volume never bypasses quality, account, or measurement gates.

claim: Do not judge a content format before a declared cohort of 20 to 30 real posts has matured.
mechanism: A minimum cohort reduces premature decisions from noisy early posts, but only native metrics and business outcomes count; posting volume without measurement teaches nothing.

claim: Keep one recognizable voice and character identity within each product-dedicated account.
mechanism: Stable voice and visual identity create recognition across repeated posts while language, script, and hook can vary within the account promise.
our_result: The current ebook-en monk lane already uses a fixed voice; this records the accepted operating rule and does not claim revenue lift.

claim: For faceless short-form videos, refresh the visual every three to five seconds and enable captions by default.
mechanism: Frequent visual changes reduce static-frame fatigue while captions preserve comprehension for sound-off viewers; test retention, completion, and shares against a slower-cut no-caption control.

claim: Test a hold-to-reveal affirmation interaction that makes the affirmation visibly glow before presenting the completed card.
mechanism: A brief press-and-hold creates a small embodied ritual and delayed reveal, potentially increasing attention and perceived participation; compare hold-to-reveal with an immediate tap reveal using completion rate, repeat sessions, and notification opens.

claim: Use version-aware App Store Connect sales and subscription report ingestion to keep product and marketing decisions tied to current revenue data.
mechanism: Automated JSON-first report retrieval with compatibility for current sales-report versions and isolated analytics HTTP tests can reduce measurement breakage between releases; compare experiment-level paywall, trial, and creative outcomes before and after adopting the pipeline.

claim: Use a local, simple-step short-form generation workflow to produce controlled batches of original Shorts and Reels variants.
mechanism: Local automation can reduce the marginal production effort for short-form variants, allowing structured tests of hooks, pacing, and topics; compare production time, publish volume, retention, completion, and downstream conversions against manually produced posts.

claim: Extend affirmation value beyond the app session through a customizable home-screen widget and shareable wallpaper or image.
mechanism: Persistent ambient surfaces increase repeated exposure and create a built-in sharing path; test widget activation, daily return rate, wallpaper creation, shares, and subscription conversion against an in-app-card-only control.

claim: Use private chat import followed by a visible relationship-temperature score as the first value moment, then gate counterfactual reply simulations and weekly insights.
mechanism: A concrete score makes invisible relationship dynamics legible while on-device processing lowers privacy friction; test import completion, score-view rate, premium conversion, repeat analysis, and refund rate against a generic advice onboarding flow.

claim: Test AI-assisted localization as an overseas affiliate-content lane for creators who lack English fluency or foreign-market expertise.
mechanism: Use an AI workflow to translate and adapt one product angle for a target market, then compare localized posts with domestic-language posts on qualified clicks, affiliate conversion, production time, and refund rate.

claim: Add currency-aware, dry-run-safe refund and sales operations to digital-product marketing workflows.
mechanism: Read the sale currency before calculating partial refunds, validate inputs locally before authenticated requests, and require dry-run protection for mutations; test operational error rate, accidental mutation rate, refund handling time, and support workload across currencies.

claim: Begin product copy with the specific moment immediately before the audience needs the product, then earn continuation before introducing the offer.
mechanism: A concrete, self-recognizable scene can create relevance and a reason to keep reading before the commercial transition; test scene-first openings against feature-first openings using hold rate, continuation rate, qualified clicks, and downstream conversion.

claim: HeyGen’s creator case says Yang Mun uses short, one-message scripts, batches videos, and moved from a few weekly posts to daily publishing.
mechanism: A recurring character and constrained script shape can reduce production work per post; the creator/provider account does not prove that cadence caused paid orders or profit.

claim: One creator-disclosed AI story video uses a five-stage visual parable: unequal treatment, accusation, reveal, reversal, and reconciliation.
mechanism: A short visual conflict followed by a legible change can deliver a complete moral story without reproducing another creator’s script; the sampled video does not show an eBook offer.

claim: The seller displays a $49.99 guided 30-day program and a $59.99 collection that adds three eBooks.
mechanism: A finite daily program and related reading are presented as one higher-priced bundle; the displayed $10 difference is not margin and the page does not expose order-level sales.
